author: c2-sql-sme-critic (independent PostgreSQL SME critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; reviewed commit 8a7daa17)

findings.claim: Activity 3 check: the task says 'Sort by course_id', but a query with no ORDER BY passes every check ('Every check is met'). The editor itself prints '(no ORDER BY: PostgreSQL does not promise this row order)' under that same output. With hash aggregation, a server may return the two groups in either order. The join pages reject a missing ORDER BY with an accurate note; this page accepts an order the server does not promise.

evidence.section: PostgreSQL 19 (current): 7.5 Sorting Rows: "If sorting is not chosen, the rows will be returned in an unspecified order ... A particular output ordering can only be guaranteed if the sort step is explicitly chosen."

findings.recommendation: When o.st.order is empty, mark the run near and add the note used on the join pages: the rows are right, but without ORDER BY PostgreSQL does not promise their order; add ORDER BY course_id.
